messages:
omar: Heads up — vendor released advisories for grpc-go and golang-jwt today. initial triage suggests a stream-handling DoS vector in grpc and malformed token parsing edge-case in the jwt lib.

julia: Thanks. Can you paste the advisory links?

omar: https://vendor.example/advisory/grpc-go (internal mirror)
omar: https://vendor.example/advisory/golang-jwt

kevin: net/http also has a reported request-parsing issue that could affect our internal control plane. not confirmed yet but worth treating as high risk.

sec-bot: Created ticket SEC-4234: "deps: grpc-go / golang-jwt / net/http - triage + mitigation" assigned to @julia + @kevin. SLA 72h.

julia: Proposed short plan: 1) pin production images to patched module versions, 2) build canary with rollout to staging + a single small fleet in prod, 3) enable extra audit logging on auth paths, 4) prepare rollback.

priya: For pinning, i'd rather use explicit module versions in go.mod and a prod-only go.sum lockfile to avoid drift. Example quick patch:

```
module github.com/redwood/inference
\nrequire (
    google.golang.org/grpc v1.56.3 // pinned
    github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.5.1 // pinned
)
\n// optional replace for hotpatch testing
replace google.golang.org/grpc => google.golang.org/grpc v1.56.3
```

kevin: That looks good. For net/http we may need a backport in our forked libraries. if upstream patch is not available for our go runtime, we should patch in the callsite (sanitize headers early).

omar: Risk matrix: auth paths (token intake, introspection) -> HIGH; internal control plane (gRPC) -> MED-HIGH; public API ingress -> MED. Prioritize accordingly.

devops-ana: Plan for canary rollout: build canary image with pinned deps, deploy to one zone, throttle traffic to 1% with routing header, monitor latency + error spikes for 2 hours, then 10% for 4 hours. If no red flags, proceed to full. Metric hooks: 5xx on auth, rpc stream resets, token parse errors.

julia: Also enable additional audit logs for token validation paths (log token header hashes only, never raw token). update RBAC so only auth-service writes those audit entries. KMS: ensure key rotations won't fail token verification; we should run a key-rotation dry-run in staging before rollout.

priya: KMS checklist: 1) confirm signer public keys cached in services, 2) increase retry/backoff window for remote KMS calls during rollout, 3) add metric for KMS failures -> alert P1.

kevin: Are we okay doing a hotpatch release on stable branch? we might need backports to older releases that customers still run. i can draft PRs for v1.2.x and v1.3.x branches.

omar: yes draft PRs. label as "security/hotpatch" and include CVE text in changelog. communicate to customer success if we need them to upgrade pinned versions.

julia: Quick commands for devs testing locally:
```
# update module locally
go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.56.3
go get github.com/golang-jwt/jwt@v4.5.1
go mod tidy
```

priya: dev note: when testing JWT fixes, use long-lived malformed tokens generator so we can reproduce parser edgecases. avoid sending real user tokens to staging.

devops-ana: I'll wire an alert: prometheus rule for "auth_token_parse_errors > 5/min" -> page on-call. Also configure temporary 7d retention for related audit logs.

sec-bot: SEC-4234 status changed -> in_progress (julia).

omar: OK folks — owners: julia (triage + PRs), kevin (backports), devops-ana (canary + alerts), priya (KMS + test harness). target: staged canary within 36h, prod rollout in 72h if green. Postmortem doc after complete.

julia: I'll open the three PRs and post links here when ready. thanks all. :thumbsup:
